title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
oneLinerQuestion: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in an array.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) problem requires finding the length of the longest subsequence in an array such that all elements are strictly increasing. Because any element can potentially extend an increasing subsequence formed by earlier elements, the optimal solution exhibits optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems suitable for dynamic programming. We define a 1D DP table where `dp[i]` represents the length of the longest increasing subsequence that ends strictly at index `i`. Every element can form a subsequence of length 1 by itself, establishing our base state. For every subsequent index `i`, we scan all preceding indices `j < i`: whenever `nums[j] < nums[i]`, `nums[i]` can legally extend any subsequence ending at `j`, allowing us to update `dp[i] = max(dp[i], 1 + dp[j])`.

- Step 1: Base Case & Edge Checking — If `nums.length === 0`, return `0`. If `nums.length === 1`, return `1`.

- Step 2: DP Table Initialization — We allocate an array `dp = new Array(nums.length).fill(1)`. Every individual element forms a valid increasing subsequence of length 1 independently.

- Step 3: Outer Loop Subproblem Traversal — We iterate through `nums` from left to right using index `i` from `1` to `nums.length - 1`, treating each index as the prospective terminus of an increasing subsequence.

- Step 4: Inner Loop Predecessor Comparison — For the current index `i`, we scan all previous elements using index `j` from `0` to `i - 1`. If `nums[i] > nums[j]`, an increasing transition is valid, so we update: `dp[i] = Math.max(dp[i], 1 + dp[j])`.

- Step 5: Global Optimum Aggregation — After evaluating all predecessor combinations for index `i`, `dp[i]` holds the length of the longest increasing subsequence terminating at `i`.

- Step 6: Termination & Maximum Extraction — Once both loops finish, the longest increasing subsequence of the entire array is the maximum value found anywhere in the DP table: `return Math.max(...dp)`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N^2) where N is the length of `nums`, as the nested loops require scanning all pairs (i, j) with 0 <= j < i < N (can be optimized to O(N log N) using patient sorting with binary search). Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space to maintain the 1D DP table of length N.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION lengthOfLIS(nums):
    LIS = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(LENGTH(nums), INITIAL_VALUE = 1)
    FOR i FROM LENGTH(nums) - 1 DOWN TO 0 DO:
        FOR j FROM i + 1 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
            IF nums[i] < nums[j] THEN LIS[i] = MAX(LIS[i], 1 + LIS[j])
        END FOR
    END FOR
    RETURN MAX(LIS)
END FUNCTION
